video_specification.overview:
Produce a {DURATION_SECONDS}-second {TONE} video about {TOPIC}. The final deliverable is a rendered MP4 at {WIDTH}x{HEIGHT} {FPS}fps generated by Remotion, with narration synthesized via ElevenLabs TTS and a timing track where every declared anchor (scene transitions, narration segment boundaries, music beats) is frame-accurate within ±1 frame.
Visual style: {VISUAL_STYLE}. The video must feel intentional — every cut should land on a narration beat or a declared anchor, not drift.

prerequisites.environment_setup: - ELEVENLABS_API_KEY is exported in the shell environment - ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID optionally overrides the default voice (Rachel) - Node 20+ and pnpm are available - The Remotion project is pre-scaffolded at the project root with: package.json (deps: remotion, @remotion/cli, vitest, typescript) src/Root.tsx (Composition registry — currently empty) src/anchors.ts (exports resolveAnchor(id): number | null) public/ (for audio.mp3 and any image assets) tsconfig.json, vitest.config.ts - Do not touch package.json dependencies unless explicitly required

technology_stack.audio_format: MP3 from ElevenLabs, served from public/audio.mp3

anchor_rules.rule: The Rule: every frame must land on its mark.

Anchors are the only synchronization points. Declare them sparingly: 4–8 scenes, at most ~6 anchors per scene. Do NOT try to synchronize every micro-animation — only scene boundaries, narration segment starts, and intentional beat drops.

Every anchor declared in timing.json must be registered in src/anchors.ts via the `resolveAnchor(id)` export. Scene components reference anchor ids — not raw frame numbers — so the alignment test can verify ±1 frame tolerance automatically.
Between anchor points, animation can breathe. Do not add extra anchors to pin intermediate motion; let interpolate/spring fill the gaps.

step.title: Phase A — Director
step.tasks: - Read video_spec.xml and produce script.json: one entry per scene with {id, narration, anchors[{id, char_offset}]} - Declare scene_status.json with one entry per scene (status=pending) - The harness driver (director.py) then runs tts.synthesize_script() which writes public/audio.mp3 and timing.json - The harness driver writes alignment.test.ts from timing.json - Director phase ends; gate: timing.json + alignment.test.ts must exist

step.title: Phase B — Scene components (parallel)
step.tasks: - For each scene, produce src/scenes/Scene{N}.tsx as a Remotion Sequence that starts at the scene's start_frame from timing.json - All keyframes, Sequence `from` props, and spring targets must be expressed as `anchors["{anchor_id}"] - sceneStart` — never as raw frame numbers - Register every anchor id in src/anchors.ts so resolveAnchor() can answer the alignment test - Update scene_status.json: pending → in_progress → aligned

step.title: Phase C — Compositor
step.tasks: - Assemble src/Root.tsx: one Composition that mounts every scene in order, wires <Audio src={`{staticFile('audio.mp3')}`} />, and sets durationInFrames = timing.total_frames, fps = timing.fps - Run `npx vitest run alignment.test.ts` — must pass - Run `npx remotion render` → out/video.mp4 - Update scene_status.json: aligned → rendered

success_criteria.functionality: - alignment.test.ts passes (every anchor within ±1 frame) - out/video.mp4 exists and plays end-to-end - Audio and visuals are synchronized at every declared anchor
success_criteria.temporal_alignment: - Scene transitions land on the frame declared in timing.json - Narration segment starts are reachable from resolveAnchor() - No scene component references raw frame numbers — only anchor ids
success_criteria.quality: - Scenes reflect the visual style declared above - Narration reads naturally and matches the scene it accompanies - No black frames, no audio gaps beyond intentional silence
